newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude closes strong on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude closes strong on fund buying.

text.p: IPE February Brent crude rallied sharply in the last hour of trade as strong fund buying re-entered the market, brokers said.
The Feb Brent contract closed on Wednesday up some 44 cents at $23.80 a barrel after "extremely choppy trading" in over a one dollar range for the day, one broker said.
The contract hit the days high of $24.10 a barrel in late trade but found some good selling at this level and lost ground.

"All the buying is fund based and New York led. The move down earlier was technically inspired and I see no news to link the turnaround (in price move) to. It's a bit of a crazy market," another broker commented.
A cold weather front approaching the eastern two-thirds of the U.S. was price supportive, but not unexpected, he added.

Renewed concern over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin was also price supportive. Yeltsin, recovering from a serious bout of pneumonia, must stay in hospital for the rest of the week because of the risk of complications, the chief Kremlin doctor said on Wednesday.

February gas oil closed earlier down some 25 cents at $213.50 a tonne after heavy selling by investment funds pushed prices lower. Based on the firm close on Brent crude and NYMEX heating oil brokers expected the contract to open up to $5-7 a tonne firmer.
